explain.say: One December night in 1773, colonists dressed as Mohawk people boarded ships in Boston harbour and dumped 342 chests of tea into the sea. It was a protest against a tax and a trading monopoly. Within three years thirteen colonies declared independence. Look at the timeline from tax to new nation.

explain.say: Why? See the chain of because. Britain had won the Seven Years' War but owed huge debts, so it taxed the colonies. Colonists had no members in Parliament, hence the slogan no taxation without representation. Then Enlightenment ideas about rights made a tax quarrel a fight about freedom. Which cause sounds most like a spark, and which like fuel?

explain.say: Now the map. Fighting began near Boston in 1775. Philadelphia hosted the Congress that declared independence. After an American victory at Saratoga in 1777, France joined in 1778, sending money, troops and a fleet. Why would France, a monarchy, help rebels against a king?

draw.text: Answer hint: revenge on Britain after losing the Seven Years' War.

explain.say: On 4 July 1776 the Declaration said all men are created equal, with rights to life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness. In 1781 a British army surrendered at Yorktown, trapped by American and French forces. In 1787 the Constitution set up a federal republic. See the Declaration light up. Whose words were these mainly?

explain.say: Now look at who gained. About 500,000 enslaved people stayed enslaved; Native nations lost land; women could not vote; many Loyalists fled. Gordon Wood called it truly radical, while others stress its limits. Well done. Challenge: name one group that read the Declaration and demanded its promise for themselves.

faq.q: Why did the American colonies rebel?
faq.a: After the Seven Years' War Britain taxed the colonies to pay its debts, through acts such as the Stamp Act of 1765. Colonists had no representatives in Parliament, and Enlightenment ideas about natural rights turned protests into a demand for independence.
asks: What does no taxation without representation mean?

faq.q: How did France help the American Revolution?
faq.a: After the American victory at Saratoga in 1777, France signed an alliance in 1778 and sent money, soldiers and a navy. A French fleet helped trap the British army at Yorktown in 1781.
asks: Why did France join the war?

faq.q: Who was left out of the American Revolution?
faq.a: Enslaved Africans, about one in five of the colonial population, mostly stayed enslaved. Native nations lost land, women could not vote, and tens of thousands of Loyalists left. Some enslaved people won freedom by joining the British side.

faq.q: Who wrote the Declaration of Independence?
faq.a: Thomas Jefferson wrote the main draft, which a committee and the Continental Congress edited. It was adopted on 4 July 1776.
asks: When was the Declaration of Independence signed?

faq.a: Colonists who stayed loyal to the British crown, perhaps a fifth of the white population. Many moved to Canada, Britain or the Caribbean after the war.

facts: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776.
The British army under Cornwallis surrendered at Yorktown in October 1781.
In the Treaty of Paris of 1783 Britain recognised American independence.
